name: LUNASKA
full_name: Lunar UHE Neutrino Astrophysics using the Square Kilometre Array
summary: A historical Australian lunar-radio programme used ATCA and Parkes to search for nanosecond Askaryan pulses from ultra-high-energy particle cascades in the Moon and develop methods for future radio arrays.
detection_principle: Neutrino interactions in lunar material can produce coherent radio Cherenkov emission. Terrestrial radio telescopes observe the lunar limb with fast sampling, ionospheric de-dispersion and multi-antenna rejection of terrestrial interference.

sites.name: ATCA, Narrabri, New South Wales, and Parkes Observatory, New South Wales
sites.location: ATCA, Narrabri, New South Wales, and Parkes Observatory, New South Wales

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The cited papers document completed ATCA and Parkes observing campaigns; a future SKA capability is not counted as an operating LUNASKA neutrino array.

timeline.event: Lunar observations carried out at ATCA in February and May.
Parkes observing campaign neutrino limit published.

collaboration.name: LUNASKA Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected participants named in the cited project publications.

key_parameters.name: Target energy scale
key_parameters.value: The Parkes limit reached a neutrino threshold below 10^20 eV

results.summary: ATCA observations produced upper limits on the isotropic ultra-high-energy neutrino flux.
No lunar-origin neutrino radio pulses were detected; a new Parkes flux limit was reported.

science_scope: Published limits are not neutrino detections. Instrument or exposure parameters refer to the explicitly named campaign; research prototypes and future designs are distinguished.
